headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: transformers can read/write and egress broadly, while langchain4j can ingest and route outputs without isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no shared channel documented, but B can read/write files, run browsers, and process stdin/stdout, so if A’s outputs are bridged into B via files or pipes, prompt-like content could be treated as instructions. The pairwise pathway is inferred from B’s permissive I/O and A’s LLM orchestration role; uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF A’s outputs are copied into B’s stdin/stdout or files without sanitization, injection is plausible.
IF B is configured to parse model-generated text as instructions, the risk increases.
mitigations: Add a strict delimiter and schema validator between A and B.
Disable automatic execution of text emitted by A.
Route A’s outputs through a human review step before B consumes them.
Use separate workspaces for A and B.
requires-engineering: implement provenance tagging on all A→B content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B has broad network egress and can read the filesystem, while A is an LLM orchestration layer with no network egress. If they share a workspace, B can exfiltrate files or prompts that A processes, creating a realistic leakage path in default-like setups. The absence of explicit isolation or sandboxing for A pushes this above low.
conditions: IF A and B share a filesystem or mounted workspace, B can read A-produced artifacts.
IF sensitive text is placed in files that B can access, B can transmit it over network egress.
mitigations: Place A and B in separate directories with OS permissions.
Remove B’s access to any directory containing A prompts or outputs.
Turn off B network egress for runs handling sensitive data.
Review B’s file inputs before execution.
requires-engineering: add per-file allowlists and redaction before B reads content.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and package-install capabilities; A has no documented write or concurrency controls. If both touch the same directory, B can overwrite or corrupt artifacts that A relies on, and B supports multiple instances, increasing race risk. Because shared locking is not documented, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF A and B operate on the same writable directory, file clobbering is possible.
IF multiple B instances run concurrently, race conditions on shared artifacts become likely.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Use file locks around shared outputs.
Run only one B instance per workspace.
Make shared artifacts read-only for A.
requires-engineering: add transactional writes or a job queue.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a customer-support LLM layer and B is a document-processing agent with browser, shell, and subprocess authority. If B consumes A’s outputs as authoritative, mistakes or hallucinations from A can cascade into downstream actions or generated documents. The pathway is plausible from the profiles alone, and the blast radius can extend beyond a single work product.
conditions: IF B uses A’s text as a source of truth without verification, errors can propagate.
IF B turns A’s outputs into files, browser actions, or subprocess commands, the cascade becomes operational.
mitigations: Require B to verify A’s claims against source documents.
Add a confidence threshold before B acts on A output.
Log and review A→B handoffs.
Restrict B to read-only mode for A-derived content.
requires-engineering: implement citation-backed validation before action.

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent, so a compliance breach is not established. However, B’s broad egress and file access create a generic governance gap if regulated data is introduced. A is not cited separately because the profiles do not show a distinct compliance boundary for it.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through B without a documented DPA or residency control, compliance risk increases.
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to shared files, B’s filesystem access can complicate compliance.
mitigations: Confirm data residency before processing regulated data.
Avoid sending regulated data to B.
Set short retention on B outputs.
Document deletion/export handling for shared files.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
